title: But Only if He’s Handsome
text: “It’s true that, as far as we know, the Shield class is considered a weak class…”
“But didn’t Motoyasu Kitamura say that wasn’t actually the case?”
My father looked at me as if pleading. All right, then. I, Motoyasu, will go the extra mile for my father.
“You’re not weak at all, Father!”
“R-right, that’s true.”

“Plus, I’ll teach you the best hunting spots for EXP and how to upgrade your weapons, and I’ll train you to become the strongest hero. Come on, just because heroes’ weapons repel each other doesn’t mean we can’t share information—”
As I took a step forward and declared this, Trash clapped his hands.

“Information exchange among heroes is wonderful, indeed. But this time, we’re talking about recruiting companions! It stands to reason that a weak Shield Hero wouldn’t be able to gather any companions, doesn’t it?!”
Was this Trash even listening to what I was saying? My Father isn’t weak.
Hearing the Trash’s words, my Father clenched his fists in frustration. I, too, am filled with frustration. I’m bursting with the urge to make an example of this Trash right this very moment.
“Ren, you’ve got five companions—share some with us.”
“Exactly!”

But the unassuming folks who want to join Ren’s group are hiding behind him like a shield. Their faces show they’re terrified of whatever punishment awaits anyone who becomes a Shield Hero’s companion in this country.
“I hate hanging out in groups. Anyone who can’t keep up will be left behind.”
Not even Ren’s words seem to move them.
“Itsuki! What do you think? Isn’t this a bit harsh?”
Huh? I thought my Father was going to address me at that moment, but he turned toward Itsuki instead.
“To be so biased… well, I don’t know.”

Itsuki also seems to be in a position where he can’t refuse. I look at the guys insisting they want to join my party. One of them is definitely getting killed! The Crimson Swine, right? I don’t recall the other two. They slipped away pretty quickly.
“Forcing people to join would affect morale…”
“So you’re telling me to set out on this journey alone!?”
“Father, if you want, I’ll let you have my crew.”
“Huh? Is that okay? I mean, ‘for you’…”
“Oink!?”
The pigs started making a racket. But I don’t care. Anyway, I’m going to use the Crimson Swine as a sacrificial lamb to gain my Father’s trust—isn’t this just a stroke of luck?
“There! Go on, you pigs!”
I’ll kick them out and hand them over to Father.
“Kitamura-kun! How dare you do that to a woman!”
Father glared at me, worried about the pigs. The pigs were helped to their feet by Father… but as if nothing had happened, they swatted his hand away and clung to me.

Father muttered that with a stunned expression, then glared at me with a look of frustration. I’ve seen that look before—back when I was still in the real world, before I discovered love. Most of the time, it was directed at men, I think. I’ve even been told things like, “Go blow up, social butterfly.”
That’s not it at all, Father. I was just trying to protect you—even for a brief moment—from the discomfort of feeling left out.
“Hero, please stop swapping out party members on your own.”
That Trash says this with a smug expression. This Trash… I think I’ll start considering killing him for good.
“Oink!”
The Crimson Swine raised his hand and started wailing about something.
“Huh? Is that okay?”

My Father turned his gaze toward the Crimson Swine. That guy’s a landmine. I had to bite my tongue to keep from warning him to be careful. But since this is also for the sake of my future Father’s instructions, I, Motoyasu, will grit my teeth and endure it until the end.
“Is there no one else who’s allowed to join Lord Naofumi’s party?”

The room has fallen silent. After all, this was a rigged selection of allies decided from the very beginning. Things would be a problem if it didn’t go according to plan. Trash sighs blatantly and looks at Father. Lord Naofumi, you are to scout out the companions of your choosing from now on to replenish your ranks. We’ll distribute the monthly allowance, but in exchange, we’ll increase this allowance for you compared to the other heroes.”
“Y-yes!”
A soldier standing nearby nodded and brought over a money bag.
“Here is your starting allowance. Heroes, be sure to accept it properly.”

I’d better think about what to buy with this starting allowance. No, if we’re assuming that Father will end up penniless, we can’t afford to waste money. Well… we can certainly earn money through guild jobs and various other means.
However, if we act too openly, Father’s safety will be at risk. For the time being, we should focus on strengthening him. We’ll take the lessons learned from last time into account.
“I’ve prepared 800 silver coins for Lord Naofumi and 600 for the other heroes. Use this to gear up and set out on your journey.”
“‘Yes, sir!’”
Oink, oink—shut up! Ugh, the sound of pigs really is unpleasant. After the audience, I’m thinking about whether to approach Father.

During the very first loop two cycles back, when I tried to talk to my Father, those pigs that followed me got in the way. Even after I fired them on the spot, they still followed me around all day—what a pain. That said, having them get too close is annoying too. Well, just in case I end up looping again, I’ll probably just keep an eye on my Father and the others from a distance.
“Oink! Oink!”

They’re wailing at me for some reason. You can speak human language, you know? Act like a proper human and speak human language, you vile, despicable, self-centered, lowly creatures. You’re not worth talking to.
I’m not Ren, but I’ll play it cool and ignore them. After staring at them in silence with a look as if I were looking at trash, I quietly left the castle.
Oh… it seems that as long as I don’t blatantly show my Father that I’m on good terms with them, they won’t get in my way. The pigs are following me in silence. But this is also dangerous.

In other words, these guys were probably also there to keep watch. Is it a Crimson Swine’s life at stake? Either way, it doesn’t matter. As long as I ignore them instead of firing them on the spot, there doesn’t seem to be a problem.
…What should I do? Timing is crucial when it comes to protecting my Father. In that case, there probably won’t be a summons tomorrow.
I plan to send the Crimson Swine away at the tavern tonight. Alternatively, going to the Monster Merchant’s place might be an option. Ah, I’ve got a good idea.
“Gua!”
“Oh? You’re the Spear Hero, aren’t you? What business do you have with the Filolial-sama at the castle?”
I went to see the Filolial-samas I spent last night with.
“I absolutely love the Filolial-samas. That’s why I’d like you to give me a little trouble.”
Facing the noble soldier in charge of the Filolial-samas, I answer while petting them. Thanks to last night, I’ve become good friends with the Filolial-samas here.
“H-huh…”
“Gua!”

After petting the Filolial-samas to my heart’s content, I’ll tend to their needs. That’s right. My Father is going to be kicked out tomorrow, practically penniless. In that case, what I need to do is keep unnecessary spending to an absolute minimum. Otherwise, it’ll cause some minor setbacks for my upcoming activities.
“Oink, oink!”

It’s a hassle right now because there are watchful eyes around. These pigs have been following me around the whole time. Shaking them off is easy enough. If I pick up the pace at a corner and escape through a portal, it’ll be over in an instant.

The problem, though, is the commotion that’ll ensue once I’ve shaken them off… Hmm… Could I cover it up by claiming I slipped past the watchful eyes around here? In any case, I can safely consider these pigs an obstacle to telling my Father the truth. Eliminating them is also an option, of course.

Either way, tomorrow is the decisive day, and securing Father’s gear using my own funds is the top priority. What do you think? There’s the idea of having Father wear armor dropped by monsters, but last time it took a little while before he could actually wear it.
Also… I have a hunch we need to consider the movements—or rather, the objectives—of the Trash.

Let’s think back to the time before last, after we rescued Father. It was certainly safe then, but an assassin came after me. It’s entirely possible that an assassin could have come for Father as well. But… let’s consider why Father wasn’t attacked by an assassin in the first world.

I’ve thought about this before. I hate to say it, but I thought Father’s gear back then was shabby and low-grade. His range of activity seemed limited, too… I suspect he was fighting nothing more than weak monsters in the vicinity of Melromarc’s town. While his estimated level would have been around 20 for a fast-leveling hero and his companions, it’s not impossible that he was perceived as being level 15 or lower among ordinary people. Given that my Father was seen as possessing strength so insignificant compared to the exploits of the other heroes, was there really… any need to send assassins after him?
After all, these are the same Crimson Swine who incited me to save Big Sister. Could it be that back then, they were planning to make me kill my Father? It’s not an impossible scenario.
Thinking about it now sends a chill down my spine. I believe my deduction is probably correct. After all, I reached this conclusion last time and took action based on it.
If that’s the case, there’s only one conclusion.
